meaning: よ / ね · new information vs shared ground
gist: よ and ね go at the very end of a sentence, after です or ます. よ tells the listener something they don't know: この[店|みせ]は[安|やす]いですよ. ね marks something you both know or feel, or a fact you want to check: [今日|きょう]は[暑|あつ]いですね. よね asks the listener to confirm what you think is true: [明日|あした]は[休|やす]みですよね.

rows: この[店|みせ]は[安|やす]いですよ。
[電車|でんしゃ]が[来|き]ますよ。
[今日|きょう]は[暑|あつ]いですね。
[明日|あした]のテストは[九時|くじ]ですね。
です / ます + よね
[田中|たなか]さんも[来|き]ますよね。
formation.note: よ and ね come last, after です or ます. When both appear, the order is always よね, never ×ねよ. In casual speech they attach to plain forms: [高|たか]いよ / [暑|あつ]いね / [学生|がくせい]だよ.

explanation: よ and ね go at the very end of a sentence. They show whether the listener already knows what you are saying. よ marks something the listener doesn't know yet, such as news, a tip, a warning, or a correction. この[店|みせ]は[安|やす]いですよ passes on something useful. ね marks shared ground. It can be a feeling you expect the listener to share ([今日|きょう]は[暑|あつ]いですね), or a fact you want to check ([明日|あした]のテストは[九時|くじ]ですね). よね joins the two. You think something is true, and you ask the listener to agree: [田中|たなか]さんも[来|き]ますよね. In polite speech, the particle follows です or ます. The usual reply to a ね sentence is そうですね (Yes, it is). Getting the choice wrong changes the feel. よ on something the listener can plainly see sounds like a lecture. A sentence of small talk without ね can sound cold.

senses.label: よ · telling the listener something new
senses.body: News, a tip, or a warning the listener doesn't have yet.
senses.example_ruby: この[店|みせ]のケーキはおいしいですよ。
senses.example_en: The cake at this shop is good, you know.

senses.label: よ · correcting
senses.body: Gives the right information when the listener has it wrong.
senses.example_ruby: いいえ、[今日|きょう]は[月曜日|げつようび]ですよ。

senses.label: ね · shared feeling
senses.body: You expect the listener to feel the same way.
senses.example_ruby: [今日|きょう]は[寒|さむ]いですね。

senses.label: ね · checking a fact
senses.body: You confirm something you already heard or expect.
senses.example_ruby: [明日|あした]のテストは[九時|くじ]ですね。
senses.example_en: Tomorrow's test is at nine, right?

senses.label: よね · asking for agreement
senses.body: You think it is true and want the listener to confirm.
senses.example_ruby: [田中|たなか]さんも[来|き]ますよね。

register_context: Polite: よ / ね follow です or ます: [高|たか]いですよ / [行|い]きますね. Casual speech attaches them to plain forms: [高|たか]いよ / [暑|あつ]いね / [学生|がくせい]だよ. ね is friendly and very common in small talk. The usual reply is そうですね. よ is useful but strong. Used too often, or with a teacher or boss, it can sound like you are lecturing them. Leave よ off facts the listener obviously knows.

mistakes.why: When both appear, the order is よね. ×ねよ is wrong.
In polite speech, よ comes after です, at the very end. ×よです puts it in the middle.

mistakes.wrong_ruby: [今日|きょう]はいい[天気|てんき]ですよ。(Meaning: said to someone outdoors with you, as if it were news.)
mistakes.right_ruby: [今日|きょう]はいい[天気|てんき]ですね。
mistakes.why: The listener can see the weather too, so it is shared ground. Use ね.

mistakes.wrong_ruby: [駅|えき]の[前|まえ]に[新|あたら]しいカフェがありますね。(Meaning: telling a friend news, as if they already knew it.)
mistakes.right_ruby: [駅|えき]の[前|まえ]に[新|あたら]しいカフェがありますよ。
mistakes.why: Your friend doesn't know about the café yet, so it is news. Use よ.

contrasts.label: よ vs ね
contrasts.summary: よ gives the listener new information. ね assumes they know or feel it too.
contrasts.ex_a_ruby: この[店|みせ]は[安|やす]いですよ。
contrasts.ex_a_en: This shop is cheap, you know. (news for the listener)
contrasts.ex_b_ruby: この[店|みせ]は[安|やす]いですね。
contrasts.ex_b_en: This shop is cheap, isn't it? (you both see the prices)

contrasts.label: か vs ね
contrasts.summary: か asks a real question. ね checks something you already expect is true.
contrasts.ex_a_ruby: [田中|たなか]さんは[学生|がくせい]ですか。
contrasts.ex_b_ruby: [田中|たなか]さんは[学生|がくせい]ですね。

contrasts.label: No particle vs よ
contrasts.summary: Without a particle, the sentence just states a fact. よ points it at the listener as something they should know.
contrasts.ex_b_ruby: [電車|でんしゃ]が[来|き]ますよ。

contrasts.label: ね vs よね
contrasts.summary: ね checks a fact or shares a feeling. よね leans on the listener a little more: you think it is true and want them to agree.
contrasts.ex_a_ruby: [明日|あした]は[休|やす]みですね。
contrasts.ex_b_ruby: [明日|あした]は[休|やす]みですよね。
contrasts.ex_b_en: Tomorrow's a day off, isn't it? (asking you to confirm)

examples.english: The cake at this shop is good, you know.

いいえ、[今日|きょう]は[月曜日|げつようび]ですよ。
その[映画|えいが]はあまり[面白|おもしろ]くないですよ。
examples.english: That movie isn't very good, you know.

examples.ruby: [今日|きょう]は[寒|さむ]いですね。
きれいな[花|はな]ですね。
[日本語|にほんご]が[上手|じょうず]ですね。
[明日|あした]のテストは[九時|くじ]ですね。
examples.english: Tomorrow's test is at nine, right?

examples.ruby: [田中|たなか]さんも[来|き]ますよね。
このラーメン、おいしいね。
examples.english: (Casual, to a friend) This ramen is good, huh.

dialogue.english: Really? I don't have an umbrella.

checks.prompt: Telling a friend news they don't know: あの店は安いです（　）。
checks.why: The listener doesn't know yet, so it is news: よ.

checks.prompt: Standing outside together on a hot day: 今日は暑いです（　）。
checks.why: You both feel the heat, so it is shared ground: ね.
The order is よね, and it comes after です.

checks.prompt: A: 今日は寒いですね。 B: （　）
checks.why: そうですね agrees with a ね sentence. Asking 寒いですか back is odd, and ×ねよ is the wrong order.

checks.prompt: A: 今日は火曜日ですね。 B: いいえ、月曜日です（　）。
checks.why: B corrects A, which gives A new information: よ.
